key_insight: Identical behavior can hide different integrated information, while finite experiments can certify lower bounds only with suitable access to a system’s internal mechanisms.
engineering_relevance: Mechanism-level AI audits must choose interventions and recordings carefully, because behavioral agreement and accurate surrogate predictions do not guarantee accurate integrated-information estimates.
method: Analyze identifiability and continuity of integrated information φ in stochastic four- and five-unit networks.
Compare behavioral observations, partial internal recordings and targeted interventions against known ground truth.
Construct finite-data lower-bound certificates with controlled false-certificate probability.
evidence_signal: Behavior-matched networks had φ values of 0.28 and 0 bits; internal recordings distinguished them in 4–53 trials, and about 10^7 controlled transitions certified φ > 1.004 bits across a 64-dimensional mechanism region.
watch_item: Results concern small, controlled networks; partial access creates irreducible uncertainty, and discontinuities can make precise point estimates fragile.
paper_title: Same Behavior, Different Mechanism: What Finite Experiments Can Certify About Integrated Information
